system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal. Seller material treated as counterparty draft, not as agreed terms.

## Headline

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced" and refers to "key negotiated positions". Nothing in it has been negotiated or agreed by us. Several items are presented as settled (the 20% cap, the 18-month period, the "general regime" for tax/IP) when they either match a fallback we have **no authority** to use, or go well beyond anything in our playbook. The Disclosure Letter is, by contrast, quite candid – and almost every candid admission in it confirms a point we need to push back on in the SPA. We should use the Disclosure Letter against the SPA draft.

Departures fall into three tiers:

- **Tier 1 – reject outright (structural):** collapse of fundamental/title into the general regime; "all Claims" override; no fraud carve-out; blanket buyer-knowledge bar; whole-data-room disclosure.
- **Tier 2 – reject on numbers / mechanics:** cap, thresholds, time period, Riverlark post-completion release, Bluefen consent-on-delivery, bonuses omitted from funds flow.
- **Tier 3 – hold open / seek information:** Ironquay, DD-006 incident, Sandbar, tax/IP, title evidence.

---

## Tier 1 – Structural departures

### 1. Fundamental / Title warranties folded into general regime
**Seller:** capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
**Playbook:** separate regime – 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
**Reasoning:** This is the single most damaging item. If the Seller doesn't actually own the shares, or lacks capacity, we lose the entire AUD 24m purchase yet recover at most 20% (or 25%) and only if we notice within 18/24 months. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason; there is nothing complex about a second column in the limitation schedule. Note the Disclosure Letter item 10 expressly says title relies on the Company's own register and that we have not verified it – which is exactly why title must carry full-price, long-tail protection.
**Action:** Reject. Insert separate Fundamental Warranty regime per playbook.

### 2. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Cl 12.3/13) and "limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
**Playbook:** Keep Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override; fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carved out of everything.
**Reasoning:** These two sentences are a general-regime override by drafting default. Read literally they would subject the specific Ironquay indemnity, any tax indemnity, completion payment obligations, restrictive covenants and even fraud claims to the 20% cap, the AUD 250k basket and the 18-month limit. The exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language applied to "Claims of any nature" would also purport to exclude claims for fraudulent misrepresentation and misleading or deceptive conduct – a position which is both commercially unacceptable and, in respect of fraud and statutory claims, of doubtful enforceability under NSW law in any event. Note the draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**; its absence combined with "all Claims of any nature" is presumably not accidental.
**Action:** Reject. Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable per playbook and no one on our side can waive it.

### 3. Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (Cl 8.3)
**Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
**Playbook:** delete blanket exclusions; any knowledge qualifier must be on the Seller's side (named persons + reasonable enquiry); never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that converts every data room document into a defence, and extends it to advisers, which means privileged DD work product becomes a liability. Combined with Schedule 7 (below) this would effectively hollow out the warranties. It also, as drafted, applies to title and capacity.
**Action:** Delete. If a knowledge concept survives anywhere, it is the Seller's knowledge qualifier on specific operational warranties, defined by named individuals after due enquiry.

### 4. General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
**Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Reasoning:** DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room, and 1.2 adds the statutory registers and public records. "Referred to in" is wider still than "contained in". With a 100% share deal and a data room of unknown depth, this makes the warranties largely illusory and shifts the diligence risk entirely onto us.
**Action:** Replace with a fair-disclosure standard: disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data room documents are disclosed only to the extent specifically cross-referenced. Public registers not deemed disclosed. Also reject DL 1.4's blanket "nothing admits anything" to the extent it is intended to limit the effect of the specific disclosures themselves – a disclosure can't both count as disclosure and deny it describes anything.

---

## Tier 2 – Numbers and mechanics

### 5. General warranty cap (Cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% figure is a fallback requiring **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft – none given**.
**Action:** Respond at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is in range. Flag internally that the Seller has (coincidentally or otherwise) landed on our undisclosed fallback; the team should check nothing has been communicated that implies it.

### 6. Thresholds (Cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
**Reasoning:** Each number is 5x our position, and the excess-only ("deductible") mechanism means the Seller never pays the first AUD 250k of any loss. On a business with ~AUD 12m revenue, a AUD 25k de minimis excludes most realistic operational claims.
**Action:** Counter at playbook figures; insist on tipping (first-dollar) basket.

### 7. Claims period (Cl 12.3): 18 months
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval – none given.
**Reasoning:** 24 months captures two audit cycles and two financial year-ends; 18 does not. Tax should in any case run to the statutory review period plus margin; see item 14.
**Action:** Counter at 24 months.

### 8. Bluefen consent (Cl 3 / 6.3)
**Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Disclosure Letter 2:** ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; consent clause 11.2 carries conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions satisfied**.
**Playbook:** effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Reasoning:** The Seller's own disclosure confirms the consent is conditional and that neither the consent nor the condition evidence exists. "Satisfied on delivery" would let a conditional, unperformed consent satisfy the CP; we would complete and then discover the 11.3 conditions were never met, leaving Bluefen free to walk. This is 30% of revenue.
**Action:** CP must require (a) unconditional written consent from Bluefen, or (b) consent plus documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied, in each case in form reasonably acceptable to Buyer, delivered before Completion. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" with specific steps. Ask for the Bluefen contract (DD-002) 11.3 conditions list now so we can specify the evidence required.

### 9. Riverlark facility (Cl 2 / 7)
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter 3:** not repaid; no final discharge of security; change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2.
**Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases at Completion; a post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
**Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If security is not released at Completion we are buying a company whose assets remain charged for AUD 3.2m, with a change-of-control default (cl 8.1) crystallising on the share transfer itself. A promise of a future release is unsecured comfort from the party who will have just received AUD 24m.
**Action:** Require: payout letter from Riverlark dated within [2] business days of Completion; repayment direct from the Completion funds flow; executed deed of release and PPSR discharge (and any real-property or specific security releases) delivered at Completion, or at minimum a bank-issued irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt. Even the undertaking route needs Amelia Frost sign-off – we should not offer it in the first response.

### 10. Employee completion bonuses – DD-005 AUD 420,000
**Seller:** "a matter for the Seller", not itemised.
**Disclosure Letter 5:** AUD 420k conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
**Playbook:** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Reasoning:** "A matter for the Seller" means nothing if the obligor is the Company, which it almost certainly is (employment is with Paperbark). The cash leaves the Company we own post-Completion. Being silent on on-costs is the tell: payroll tax and superannuation on AUD 420k of bonus could be material in addition. The Seller's own disclosure concedes the omission.
**Action:** Add a line item in the funds flow: gross bonuses plus employer super, payroll tax and any other triggered on-costs, funded by the Seller (either deducted from the price as Transaction Expenses/Debt or paid by Seller to Company at Completion). Request the DD-005 schedule with the on-cost calculation. If the Seller wants them treated as Seller's own, the SPA should say so expressly with a Seller indemnity.

---

## Tier 3 – Hold open / information required

### 11. Ironquay IP (Cl 11.1)
**Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
**Disclosure Letter 4:** IP in SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open but not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; treat the AUD 180k as unverified either way.
**Reasoning:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180k invoice – it is that the Company may not own the Project Materials at all until every fee is paid. An indemnity for "the SOW3 payment" covers the cheapest outcome and none of the consequential ones (lack of title to deliverables, inability to license on, third-party claims, re-development cost).
**Action:** Broaden to cover all Loss arising from non-ownership or defective transfer of SOW3 Project Materials and any Ironquay claim; preserve the cure path (Seller to procure payment of all outstanding fees and a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion as a Completion deliverable). Do not concede or assert the AUD 180k figure; ask for Ironquay's statement and the Company's payment records.

### 12. Export / privacy incident – DD-006 (Cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
**Seller:** preliminary, "not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter 6:** link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope or whether notification required.
**Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
**Reasoning:** The facts are genuinely open and we should not overstate them. But "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the Seller has told us it cannot yet support. 1,240 business-contact records is unlikely to be catastrophic, but eligible-data-breach assessment obligations run on a clock, and if the investigation lapses between signing and Completion we inherit the problem.
**Action:** Covenant that the Seller procures: preservation of access/download logs; completion of a documented investigation (whether the link was accessed; whether the recipient has confirmed deletion); written updates at agreed intervals and a final report before Completion; Buyer consultation before any regulator/individual notification decision. Specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident, uncapped by the general regime, sized once facts are known. We do not allege breach or seek a price adjustment at this stage.

### 13. Sandbar renewals – AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
**Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure Letter 8:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Reasoning:** Both sides are asserting characterisation without evidence. The disclosure letter's statement that they should be "read together for timing/scope" suggests a split that may be designed to stay under some threshold. We need the terms.
**Action:** Request the three contracts, invoice dates and payment terms. Confirm whether any amount is accrued at the Locked Box/Completion Accounts date; if so, it belongs in Working Capital or Debt per the definitions. No price position yet.

### 14. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
**Playbook:** OPEN; no unlimited liability but no resolution.
**Reasoning:** The Seller is attempting to close these by assertion. Tax warranties under an 18-month, 20%-capped, AUD 250k-basket regime are of little value given ATO review periods. IP warranties interact directly with the Ironquay issue.
**Action:** Respond that tax and IP remain open and will be dealt with in a separate schedule. We should table a tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, full price cap, period aligned to statutory amendment windows plus margin) and IP warranties with a longer period; neither at unlimited liability.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Seller:** register evidences 100%.
**Disclosure Letter 10:** register is the source relied upon; Buyer has not verified.
**Playbook:** independent evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
**Action:** Seek: current ASIC extract and historical company search; share certificates; chain-of-title documents for all transfers since incorporation; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller; director/shareholder resolutions and constitution authority for the sale; Seller's own corporate authority evidence. This is also why item 1 must be won.

### 16. Minor – Lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)
These appear benign on the Seller's description (notification only; assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale). Confirm by reviewing the underlying clauses ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation; add the lease notification to the Completion steps.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/Title regime | Folded into general cap/time | **Reject.** Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 yrs, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |
| 2 | "All Claims" override / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Apply to all Claims of any nature | **Reject.** Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims; express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from everything |
| 3 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket, incl. "discoverable" and advisers | **Delete.** Seller knowledge qualifier only, named persons + enquiry |
| 4 | Disclosure (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + public registers | **Reject.** Specific fair disclosure only |
| 5 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. No authority for 20% |
| 6 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess-only | 5k / 50k / first-dollar |
| 7 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months. No authority for 18 |
| 8 | Bluefen CP | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | Effective consent + evidence of 11.3 conditions, pre-Completion |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion |
| 10 | DD-005 bonuses | Not itemised | Specific line item incl. on-costs, Seller-funded |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Broaden to ownership/transfer Loss; cure via payment + assignment as Completion deliverable |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Preservation/investigation/update covenants; specific indemnity; no breach assumed |
| 13 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Request documents; assess against WC/Debt definitions; no deduction yet |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | Remain OPEN; separate schedule; no unlimited liability |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence: ASIC, certificates, chain of title, PPSR, authority |

**Authority flags for Amelia Frost:** none of the fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release with undertaking) should be offered in our mark-up. If the deal team wants to table any of them later, written approval identifying the specific draft is required first.

**Immediate information requests to Seller:** Bluefen cl 11.3 conditions and consent status; Riverlark payout letter and security schedule; DD-005 bonus schedule with on-costs; Ironquay account statement and payment records; DD-006 investigation plan and log preservation confirmation; the three Sandbar contracts; title pack per item 15.

If useful, I can turn this into a numbered issues list in the Seller's clause order for the formal mark-up, or draft the replacement clauses for items 1–4 and 8–10.
=== END ADVICE ===
